title: The Welfare Food (Amendment) (England and Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Welfare Food Regulations 1996 (S.I. 1996/1434) (“the 1996 Regulations”). The 1996 Regulations provide for a scheme (the “Nursery Milk Scheme”) which entitles children under the age of five years to one-third of a pint of milk (189ml) on any day where they are provided with childcare, by an approved childcare provider, for two hours or more. Regulations 3 to 10 amend the 1996 Regulations to replace references to day care with childcare and to update references to childcare legislation in England and Wales which have been updated since the 1996 Regulations came into force. These include changes made by the Childcare Act 2006 (c. 21) for England, and the Children and Families (Wales) Measure 2010 (nawm 1) and the Child Minding and Day Care Exceptions (Wales) Order 2010 (S.I. 2010/2839) (W.233)) for Wales. These Regulations also extend eligibility under the Nursery Milk Scheme to childcare providers registered with Childminder Agencies. title: The Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) (Amendment No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make amendments to the Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2682) (“the PAYE regulations”) to make loans and living accommodation a “specified benefit” for the purposes of Chapter 3A of the PAYE regulations and provide methods for calculating their cash equivalent or the relevant amount for the purposes of the PAYE regulations. This allows employers to apply to HMRC to become an “authorised employer” under regulation 61C of the PAYE regulations in respect of loans and living accommodation for the tax year 2027-28 onwards. These Regulations have no effect for the purposes of regulation 61C(4) and (5) (applications to become an authorised employer during a tax year) until the tax year 2027-28.

title: HA appeals to public for a patient requiring urgent liver transplant
summary: The following is issued on behalf of the Hospital Authority: The spokesperson for the Hospital Authority (HA) today (October 15) made the following appeal regarding a patient whose condition requires urgent liver transplant: A 13-year-old boy who requires an urgent liver transplant is currently hospitalised at Queen Mary Hospital and is in serious condition. The patient has been experiencing severe hepatic failure and developed severe complications including recurrent hyperammonemia and cholangitis. The patient is clinically assessed as requiring an urgent liver transplant and is listed at the top of the liver transplant waiting list for O+ blood group. In response to the urgent appeal from the patient's family, the HA appeals to members of the public to proactively support organ donation and consider donating the organ of a deceased relative to rekindle the lives of others. In view of the critical condition of the patient, in addition to proactively searching for a suitable liver locally, the HA will also seek assistance from the Mainland through the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government as soon as possible. Mr Chan attended a high-level roundtable co-organised by the IMF and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) to explore how economies in the Middle East and Central Asia can better benefit from the vast opportunities offered by Hong Kong's investment and financing markets. Heads of finance ministries and central banks from a number of countries in these regions took part. In his keynote speech, Mr Chan said that the increasingly close financial ties between Hong Kong and the Middle East and Central Asia help investors diversify their investments and enable enterprises to better raise capital for business development and manage risks. As these economies continue to develop and diversify, Hong Kong can support their growth in three areas: mobilising long-term capital, broadening currency options, and managing and sharing risks. title: Government announces quarterly land sale programme for October to December 2026
summary: The Government announced today (October 15) the quarterly land sale programme for the third quarter of 2026-27, i.e. October to December 2026. The Secretary for Development, Ms Bernadette Linn, said the Government will put up for tender a site at the Junction of Tai Chung Kiu Road and On Sum Street, Shek Mun, Shatin, for private residential development in the third quarter of the 2026-27 financial year. The site has a floor space of around 48 090 square metres and can provide around 960 flats. The site is situated in a mature residential neighbourhood and in close proximity to Shek Mun MTR Station, with comprehensive surrounding infrastructure and traffic network. Originally zoned for commercial use, the site is selected from the Annual Land Sale List announced in February this year and has obtained planning approval from the Town Planning Board for private residential development.
